strategies.one_line: Treat the question 'should we disagree with the price here?' as the prediction problem. Make the market mid an expert in an online stacker and route by lifecycle and price cell. Monetise the residual as maker skew, especially in the first hours of new and toss-up markets.

strategies.name: Arena-score nowcasting: simulate the pairwise-vote mechanism that settles the monthly 'best AI model' markets
strategies.one_line: Run your own judge-model pairwise battles between a new release and the incumbents, fit Bradley-Terry with the leaderboard's own uncertainty, and price where a low-vote Arena score will converge by the monthly snapshot.
strategies.scope: Cover the recurring 'Which company has the best AI model end of <month>?' family. Rules fetched today: the market resolves on the arena.ai Text Arena Overall board with style control OFF, checked at 12:00 ET on the last day of the month. Rank decides, ties go to Arena score, and AutoEval-marked models are excluded. The file needs two layers. (1) Statistics only: turn the published score, CI and vote count into P(rank flip by snapshot) as votes accumulate. New entrants sit near 5k votes at +/-8-9, while incumbents sit at 40-75k votes at +/-3-4. (2) Simulated votes: a cross-family judge panel battles the new model against incumbents on an Arena-like prompt mix. Length and markdown preference must be reproduced, not removed, because the market uses the no-style-control board. The output is a forecast of the converged score before the leaderboard has enough votes. Add release-calendar OSINT, the lab private-testing selection effect, and vote rigging as a manipulation risk on the resolution source. State plainly that whether specialist traders already do this is unverified. Boundaries: enumerable human panels stay in critic-pool-panel-twins. Release-date markets are out of scope.

strategies.name: Outside-view engine: procedural-clock feasibility and reference-class hazards for 'by date' ladders
strategies.one_line: Compile each 'will X happen by date' market into the formal procedure that must complete, attach computed reference-class completion-time distributions, and sell rungs that are procedurally infeasible or priced above the outside-view hazard.
strategies.scope: (a) Procedure-graph extraction: steps, minimum durations and veto points for legislative calendars, treaty ratification, court scheduling, launch licensing, merger reviews and UNSC procedure. (b) Reference-class tournament: three or more candidate classes with computed base rates, not remembered ones, a red-team challenge on class membership, and a Fermi cross-check. This section should absorb the two duplicate reference-class variants now sitting in adversarial-debate-price-residual and sponsor-and-inform-niche-models. (c) Hazard term structure across the ladder: fit a constant or Weibull hazard and compare it with the market-implied one. Calendar spreads, rung k minus rung k-1, isolate 'happens in month k'. (d) Deadline-effect correction for bargaining events: agreements cluster right before the deadline, so the hazard is back-loaded, not constant. Present the negatives. Prompt-only base-rate tricks add little, so the edge has to come from the data pipeline. Insider flow dominates late in geopolitics ladders. 'Nothing ever happens' NO-buying already exists as a 987-star meme bot with no published PnL. Capital locks for months. Validation: on 60+ resolved by-date ladders after model cutoffs, compare market-implied and realised hazard by category and time-to-deadline. Then test whether 'minimum remaining procedural steps' improves log-loss over price alone. Score event-clustered.
strategies.why_it_matters: By-date ladders are among the most liquid non-sports books. The US-Iran final nuclear deal ladder has $17.84M volume, $404k liquidity and 8 rungs. In Buehler 1994 only 13% finished by their own 50% date and 45% by their 99% date. Geopolitics is fee-free, so small hazard edges are tradable. The engine is also the natural home for the list's orphaned reference-class material.

strategies.scope: An agent compiles a typed 'print spec' for each family from the rules text plus the source's methodology pages. strategies.name: Unpacking the residual: generative candidate enumeration for 'Other' and not-yet-named outcomes in augmented neg-risk events

strategies.scope: Mechanics from the docs: placeholder slots are named later via the bulletin board. 'Other' narrows as placeholders are assigned. The docs say 'Only trade on named outcomes'. The other is fast YES on newly clarified placeholders in their first hours, which links to day-zero quoting. Generator: an LLM plus structured eligibility sources (shortlists, nomination rules, filing deadlines) enumerates the unnamed field. A hierarchical prior on 'winner not currently named' is built by event type and days-to-resolution. Tie this to the list's own evidence: sub-10c purchases lose 19.3c per dollar per contract but gain 4.1c when grouped by parent event. Named longshots are individually overpriced, and the residual is the mirror image. Limits: capital lock-up, an unverified conversion fee parameter, the shifting 'Other' definition, late insider leaks and thin books. Validation step one is a pure data pull with no LLM. For every resolved augmented neg-risk event, compare how often the winner was unnamed at T-90, T-30 and T-7 with 1 minus the sum of named YES prices at those times.

strategies.name: Reward-pool minority game: simulate where rival farmers will quote tomorrow and sit where they will not
strategies.one_line: Treat liquidity-reward allocation as a repeated minority game. A population model of rival makers forecasts next-day dilution per pool, and the LP bot allocates to the best predicted reward per unit of jump risk.
strategies.scope: Data: the public /rewards/markets/multi endpoint, which worked without auth today and exposes market_competitiveness, rate_per_day, max spread and volume_24hr. Add the bot's own /rewards/user/percentages and the public distributor payout logs. Model: a heterogeneous farmer population of rate-chasers, competitiveness-chasers, category specialists and sponsored-pool sprinters. Crowd-anticrowd dynamics predict overshoot, so pools that looked empty yesterday are crowded today. Combine this with a jump-risk score built from scheduled catalysts and category gap and dispute rates, so that 'uncontested' does not mean 'gap-risk dump'. Evidence from the E2 pack, not re-fetched: 16,719 pools configured at $585k a day against $108-156k a day actually paid. Rate divided by competitiveness spans seven orders of magnitude. 23.5% of configured rate sits in competitiveness-0 markets. The top 10 wallets take 24%, and the median payout is about $5. In the Telonex case, makers doubled within a day of a sponsorship. Fetched today: five NFL moneylines with identical $15,771-a-day pools show competitiveness from 1.28 to 8.78. Validation: 30 days of hourly snapshots. First test whether the population model beats persistence at predicting next-day competitiveness. Then A/B the allocator against rate-ranked allocation, net of markout.

strategies.name: Active price probing: measure order-book resilience with small real trades and use it as the deference signal
strategies.one_line: Spend a few dollars of genuine taker flow to learn whether a price is defended by informed liquidity or is soft and stale, and let the measured resilience set how much weight the stacker gives the market.
strategies.scope: Design: randomised small marketable orders of $5-20 in both directions, held and not cancelled. Measure refill time, reversion half-life, and which maker addresses refill, taken from on-chain fills because feed direction is only about 59% accurate (E1 pack). The output is a per-market resilience score. It feeds the act-abstain gate in market-anchored-selective-deference and the LP quote width. Evidence comes from a field experiment with 5-point shocks on 817 markets. 75% of the shock remained after one week and 56% after 60 days. One-week reversion was 47% where an external estimate existed and 23% where it did not. It was 33% against 17% for above- and below-median trader counts, and 49% for above-median volume. Softness is therefore predictable, and soft prices carry the least information. The file must state that the venue was Manifold (play-money Mana, with a Sweepcash follow-up) and that no Polymarket replication exists. Validation: 100 thin markets with a randomised probe against a no-probe control. Test whether resilience predicts the later agent-versus-market Brier gap and the LP markout. The budget is a few hundred dollars of fees and spread.
strategies.why_it_matters: This is the only idea in the band where the agent creates information by interacting with the market, not by reading about the event. It answers the list's central question, 'should we disagree with the price here?', with a measurement and not a model. It is cheap, fast, and reuses the owner's execution stack. It also corrects a weakness in the list, which cites the 60-day persistence result as if it described Polymarket.
strategies.flags: Probes must be genuine risk-transferring trades. Orders placed with intent to cancel are spoofing. Self-fills breach the ToS clause on 'no change in beneficial ownership', which has no intent element (E9 pack). Never size or time probes to move thin books, trigger news citations or set off others' rules. Get a legal review before systematic use. Taker fees apply.

information-partitioned-delphi-panel: it rests on a single paper (Brier 0.216 to 0.178 on 375 questions) that was never benchmarked against the market price. decision-body-member-twins: tradable capacity is $4.3k volume on FOMC dissents. There are 8 meetings a year against a bar of roughly 350 predictions. FedSight has no futures baseline and no leakage control. Roll-call accuracy is mostly party-line. Aaru concedes Powell-class individuals cannot be simulated. Only the legislative whip-count on pivotal members has capacity plausible enough to justify the work. Merge it into the elite-selection file.

critic-pool-panel-twins, as currently scoped: RT ladders hold $2.7k-$31.6k. The entry admits humans already trade RT statistically, the twin adds nothing after 30-50 reviews, the LLM taste layer has negative evidence (super-omnivorous bias), and individual twins correlate at r=0.20. It earns a file only if widened to the large mechanically aggregated events. Eurovision 2026 shows $193.9M volume, and Oscars and audience-demand brackets add more. external-forecaster-sourcing: for tier 1, the top public agents only tie the Kalshi baseline (0.8022 against 0.7998), and anyone with real edge trades it directly. Tier 2 is token mining. Tier 3, a staked commit-reveal tournament, is legally heavy and adversely selected for a solo team. What survives is an 8-week ingestion test of one more expert inside the stacker. That is a task, not a file.

sponsor-and-inform-niche-models: the mechanism is real, since the list cites the FluSight ensemble beating disease markets so clearly that the optimal blend puts zero weight on them, against only $20.1k resting liquidity on measles. But the economics are likely negative for a small team. The one documented sponsorship cost about $70k and doubled the competing makers within a day. Farmers dilute the subsidy, other makers copy model-driven quotes, and whether the ToS allows trading a market you lobbied for and sponsored is unverified. Keep it only as a $20-a-day, 14-day experiment on an existing thin market. Drop the 'pitch a new market' branch until the ToS question is answered.

The one direct test of fading LLM consensus, on 104 World Cup matches, was unprofitable. It deserves a file only because the validation is pure logging at zero capital. If the 12-week log shows no news-free drift toward the sentinel, delete the file and do not iterate on it.

The only validated capability of OASIS-class simulators is propagation scale at about 30% NRMSE (E8 pack), which the entry does not use. Expect base-rate shrinkage to do all the work in the blind test. Pre-register 'shrunk sim equals base rate only' as the kill condition.
